title: How old are you?
goal: Count from one to twenty, say your age, and discover that nouns after numbers use a form of their own — not the plural you learned in unit 3.
bekal: count 1–20 and use numbers in front of nouns
ask and say ages with کلن and کلنه
say how many people, things, and days

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — ګلالۍ پوښتنې کوي
dialogs.intro: Gulalai, Najib's daughter, sits next to Budi holding her arithmetic book. Children are the most patient and most honest language teachers there are.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: زه اته ویشت کلن یم. او ته؟
lines.baca: zə atə-wisht kalən yəm. aw tə?
lines.literal: I eight-twenty year-old am-I. and you?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: ولې ته کلنه وایې او زه کلن؟
lines.baca: wale tə kaləna waye aw zə kalən?
lines.id: Why do you say کلنه and I say کلن?
lines.literal: why you year-old(f) say-you and I year-old?

lines.speaker: ګلالۍ:
lines.text: ځکه چې زه انجلۍ یم او تاسو سړی یاست!
lines.baca: dzəka che zə anjləy yəm aw tāso saṛay yāst!
lines.id: Because I'm a girl and you're a man!
lines.literal: because that I girl am-I and you(pl) man are-you(pl)!

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: ښه ښوونکې یې. اوس ماته شمېرې راوښیه.
lines.baca: ṣa ṣowunke ye. os mā-ta shmere rāwuṣya.
lines.id: You're a good teacher. Now show me the numbers.
lines.literal: good teacher are-you. now me-to numbers show!

lines.speaker: ګلالۍ:
lines.text: یو، دوه، درې، څلور، پنځه، شپږ، اووه، اته، نهه، لس!
lines.baca: yaw, dwa, dre, tsalor, pindzə, shpaẓ, owə, atə, nəhə, las!
lines.id: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!
lines.literal: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: ډېره ښه! ستاسو په کورنۍ کې څو کسان دي؟
lines.baca: ḍera ṣa! stāso pə kornəy ke tso kasān dī?
lines.id: Very good! How many people are there in your family?
lines.literal: very good! of-you(pl) in family in how-many people are?

lines.speaker: ګلالۍ:
lines.text: شپږ کسان. پلار، مور، انا، دوه وروڼه او زه.
lines.baca: shpaẓ kasān. plār, mor, anā, dwa wrūṇa aw zə.
lines.id: Six. Father, mother, grandmother, two brothers, and me.
lines.literal: six people. father, mother, grandmother, two brothers and I.

lines.speaker: ګلالۍ:
lines.text: یو دولس کلن دی او بل پنځلس کلن دی.
lines.baca: yaw dwolas kalən day aw bal pindzəlas kalən day.
lines.id: One is twelve and the other is fifteen.
lines.literal: one twelve year-old is and other fifteen year-old is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: زه دوه وروڼه لرم، خو هغوی په اندونیزیا کې دي.
lines.baca: zə dwa wrūṇa larəm, kho haghwī pə Indonezyā ke dī.
lines.id: I have two brothers, but they're in Indonesia.
lines.literal: I two brothers have-I, but they in Indonesia in are.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: ډېره لرې. په الوتکه کې لس ساعته لار ده.
lines.baca: ḍera lare. pə alwatka ke las sā'ata lār da.
lines.id: Very far. Ten hours by plane.
lines.literal: very far. in plane in ten hours road is.

lines.speaker: ګلالۍ:
lines.text: لس ساعته! زه یو ساعت هم نه شم ناست.
lines.baca: las sā'ata! zə yaw sā'at ham nə shəm nāst.
lines.id: Ten hours! I can't even sit still for one hour.
lines.literal: ten hours! I one hour even not can-I sit.

notes: To say your age you use the word کلن, not a verb. The sentence is زه اته ویشت کلن **یم**, literally "I eight-twenty year-old am". The word کلن behaves just like an adjective, so it agrees in gender: کلن for a male, **کلنه** for a female — exactly what Gulalai corrects in the fourth line.

Twenty-eight is اته ویشت, literally "eight twenty". Pashto says **the units first**, like German and Dutch, the reverse of English. The back of the book has the full list; unit 7 practices it at the market.

Notice the form وروڼه, not ورونه. The word ورور (brother) is one of a handful of words with an irregular plural: ورور becomes **وروڼه**, خور becomes **خویندې**, مور becomes **میندې**, زوی becomes **زامن**. These four happen to be among the most common words of all.
The word کسان means "people" and is used specifically for counting human beings. To ask how many people, the question is څو کسان دي؟ For things, just use څو with the noun.

The question څومره لرې ده؟ uses څومره, not څو. The word څو counts things you can count one by one (how many books, how many people), while څومره asks about size, price, and distance — like English "how many" versus "how much/how far". Mixing them up isn't fatal, but it sounds like asking "how many far is it".

The phrase نه شم ناست means "I can't sit". The form شم is the helper "can", and it stands **before** the main verb — one of the few things not placed at the end. Ability and permission are covered fully in unit 13.

grammars.title: Numbers 1–20, and the counting form of nouns
body: The first ten numbers have to be learned as words; the rest up to twenty are built from them with the ending **ـلس** *-las*, and the pattern is easy enough to spot even though some sounds shrink.

⚠️ A noun after a number **does not use the plural** you learned in unit 3. It uses its own counting form: کتاب becomes دوه **کتابه**, not دوه کتابونه. For feminine words ending in ه, the counting form happens to be the same as the plural: درې **ښځې**.

grammars.title: Asking and saying your age
body: The age question is always the same: څو کلن یاست؟ for a man and څو کلنه یاست؟ for a woman. Asking someone's age is not considered impolite at all in Afghanistan, even with adult women.
Notice that the gender comes from **the person being asked about**, not the one asking. Gulalai says کلنه about herself, and would say کلن about her father.

blocks.text: Pashto uses different words for counting people and for counting things, and native speakers clearly hear the difference. The table below gives you the most common forms.
The counting form: what changes after a number

blocks.title: If you forget the counting form
items: Use the plain singular. The sentence درې کتاب is still understood by everyone; it just sounds like a foreigner who hasn't been learning long — which is exactly what you are right now.
What you **must not** do is use the full plural after a number. The sentence درې کتابونه sounds wrong to a native ear, not just foreign.
For feminine words ending in ه, the plural and the counting form happen to be the same, so there is nothing to remember: درې ښځې is right both ways.

blocks.title: Numbers in everyday life
items: Phone numbers are read digit by digit, just as in English: صفر اووه نهه ... *sifr owə nəhə*.
The word صفر *sifr* means zero, and it is the source of the English words *cipher* and, through Italian, *zero*.
Eastern Arabic numerals are used alongside Western ones in Afghanistan: ۰ ۱ ۲ ۳ ۴ ۵ ۶ ۷ ۸ ۹. Notice that ۴ ۵ ۶ are written differently from the Arabic ٤ ٥ ٦ — Afghanistan uses the Persian shapes.
⚠️ Numbers are written left to right even though the script runs right to left. The year ۱۴۰۴ is read one thousand four hundred and four, not the other way round.
There are six people in our family.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: دي / کسان / شپږ / کورنۍ / کې / په

answers: تاسو څو کلن یاست؟ — زه اته ویشت کلن یم. — زمونږ په کورنۍ کې شپږ کسان دي. — زه درې کتابه لرم. — اندونیزیا ډېره لرې ده.
زه شل کلن یم. — په کورنۍ کې شپږ کسان دي. — تاسو څو کلن یاست؟ — زه درې کتابه لرم. — اندونیزیا ډېره لرې ده.
